metadata.note: Ideal step-down transformer: N_p=1980 turns, N_s=180 turns, V_p=1320V, I_p=135A. Q5ci 3m: V_s = V_p × (N_s/N_p) = 1320 × (180/1980) = 120V. Q5cii 3m: P = V_p × I_p = 1320 × 135 = 178200W = 178.2kW.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q5c(i/ii) — Transformer Output Voltage and Input Power
question.text:
An ideal step-down transformer is used as part of a power transmission system. It has 1980 turns in its primary coil and 180 turns in its secondary coil.

(i) Calculate the maximum theoretical output voltage if the input voltage is 1320 V. (3 marks)

(ii) Calculate the input power if a current of 135 A flows in the primary coil. (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q5c(i) — Output voltage:

For an ideal transformer: V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p

V_s = V_p × (N_s / N_p) = 1320 × (180 / 1980) = 1320 × (1/11) = 120 V

Check: Step-down transformer → N_s < N_p → V_s < V_p ✓ (120 V < 1320 V)

Q5c(ii) — Input power:

P = V × I = 1320 × 135 = 178 200 W = 178.2 kW

For an ideal transformer: input power = output power (100% efficiency assumed).

steps.label:
Given: N_p = 1980 turns | N_s = 180 turns | V_p = 1320 V | I_p = 135 A
Transformer ratio: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p  |  Power: P = VI

fields.label: Turns ratio N_s / N_p = _____ (as a decimal)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Turns ratio = N_s / N_p = 180 / 1980 = 1/11 ≈ 0.0909. For a step-down transformer N_s < N_p, so the ratio is less than 1.

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Use the transformer equation: V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p, rearranged as V_s = V_p × (N_s / N_p).
Use the power formula: P = V × I, where V is the primary voltage and I is the primary current.
